crates.name: rullst-macros
crates.finding: Bounded macro grammar and negative UI diagnostics now include a concrete server-function protocol: versioned typed envelopes, explicit Axum route generation, same-origin Wasm transport, body/correlation/error limits, CSRF composition, two-target Wasm compilation and generated-project evidence; real browser/network ecosystems and host identity policy remain external.

crates.name: rullst-orm-macros
crates.finding: The fail-closed structured derive parser validates duplicate and unknown options, identifiers, persisted targets and cross-field relation/embedding/soft-delete invariants through 24 exact compile-fail fixtures; broad rullst-orm runtime matrices cross-check generated behavior, while compiler/ecosystem compatibility beyond the tested matrix remains external.

crates.name: rullst-orm
crates.finding: Deep relational and tenant-bound audit/revision evidence now includes authenticated, bounded document recovery with real MongoDB-to-SurrealDB-to-MongoDB rehearsal; online snapshot isolation, managed/PITR backup, vendor operations and application writer/tenant/key policy remain external.

crates.name: rullst-core
crates.finding: The bounded runtime now couples a monotonic process lifecycle to aggregate-only readiness, fail-closed application admission and graceful in-flight drain across static/hot request paths, with an explicit supervisor shutdown trigger and poisoned-state/startup/concurrency evidence; application dependency probes, identity/domain authorization, replica consensus, load-balancer propagation and production termination operation remain explicit host boundaries.

crates.name: rullst-messaging
crates.finding: Bounded broker, canonical wire/trace, encrypted local-content rotation and ORM outbox crash-replay contracts have exact threat/restart/tamper/concurrency evidence; remote protocols, replication, full metadata encryption and provider operations remain open.

crates.name: rullst-connect
crates.finding: Substantial OAuth/OIDC protocol evidence now includes bounded provider/account-bound encryption plus a fixed-schema shared-local SQLite token store with persisted quota, exact generation CAS, restart/contention/corruption negatives and public/facade integration. Remote-provider leases and losing-call reconciliation, key/directory/backup operations, multi-host replication and formal provider conformance remain external/application work.

crates.name: rullst-iot
crates.finding: The no_std surface now includes typed bounded MQTT 5 PUBLISH and CoAP request encoders plus a signed-manifest gate with an explicit durable monotonic-CAS adapter; deterministic protocol vectors and OTA restart/failure evidence do not replace concrete transport, hardware storage, flashing, bootloader or device fault-injection.

crates.name: rullst-security
crates.finding: Broad bounded defense-in-depth plus compatible unsigned and opt-in HMAC-chained local SIEM journals with rotation, restart, forgery, quota and external-change evidence; trusted tail checkpoints, external SIEM delivery, independent audit and certification remain external.

crates.name: rullst-ai
crates.finding: Strong guarded/offline/provider boundaries plus bounded local audit, authenticated remote audit export and strict opt-in OpenAI-compatible SSE with provider-independent output limits and explicit cancellation; non-compatible streaming, live adaptive evals, durable audit receiver/provider loops and broad external retrievers remain partial.

crates.name: rullst-capital
crates.finding: Bounded payments share a redacted classified egress contract with real fault fixtures; quotas and relational webhook claims add transaction/four-protocol evidence. Signed-tpAmb binding plus a bounded HMAC-chained local fiscal command journal prove idempotent prepared/terminal transitions, restart recovery, tamper/conflict/quota failure and external checkpoints without enabling live authorization. Provider acceptance, authoritative outbox/reconciliation, multi-writer operations and homologation remain external.

crates.name: rullst-mail
crates.finding: Bounded transports, preflight, static inspection, durable shared-local suppression and minimized delivery observations; provider webhook conformance, authoritative malware inspection, multi-host operations, acceptance and inbox delivery remain open.

crates.name: rullst-auth
crates.finding: Strong password/session/RBAC/JWT primitives plus bounded shared SQLite JWT revocation and passkey device lifecycle with restart, quota, replay and counter-CAS evidence; shared ceremonies, multi-host replication, refresh workflow and normative WebAuthn conformance remain external or incomplete.

crates.name: rullst-nexus
crates.finding: Fail-closed admin with bounded metadata/forms, opt-in trusted-context tenant scoping across every built-in CRUD and batch path, generic database failures and transaction-coupled minimized mutation audit; host identity/domain policy, global-model/custom-route authorization, immutable audit delivery and production operations remain external.

crates.name: rullst-studio
crates.finding: The viewer remains verified-loopback-only while each distinct push-only route binds one producer name/key and authenticates bounded attribute-free trace batches with exact-body HMAC, clock and atomic replay checks; query findings are explicit heuristics, and memory/live-Redis cache inspection exposes opaque metadata plus one-entry local invalidation without values, exact keys or bulk flush. Durable/OTLP storage, producer key operations, shared Studio identity/RBAC/TLS and production topology remain external.

crates.name: rullst
crates.finding: All 45 public umbrella features have isolated compile boundaries with automatic manifest-drift detection, and the packaged-distribution consumer derives the complete extracted feature set instead of maintaining a partial allowlist; release confidence still inherits the bounded maturity of opt-in domain capabilities.

crates.name: cargo-rullst
crates.finding: All 270 structurally supported project profiles are materialized without path/manifest drift; a minimal eight-case matrix executes generated tests across every blueprint, hot/non-hot and release boundaries, and constructs each hot router. Five public-CLI profiles verify distinct database/frontend/AI/Redis/polyglot feature axes, with runtime delegated only where adapter matrices are stronger. Process tests cover v5/v6/v11 upgrade rules, multi-member rollback, retained-failure restore and symlink rejection. Provider accounts, deployment targets and real application acceptance remain external.
